source.quote:
Flickertail, Lake Moraine, Wildfang and Yanktonai Refuges were
virtually abandoned during this period because of previously damaged
structures and the subsequent loss of -ymter. The stuctures are ir­
reparable with the limited appropriations for easement refuges. The
signs and posts were removed from the above refuge boundaries. On
the remaining refuges the structures were repaired or remained in a
generally good condition. Most of the refuges were reposted and
damaged signs replaced by new ones.

counterevidence_checked.issue: July1,1939 Agriculture-to-Interior administrative transfer considered as earlier cessation candidate
counterevidence_checked.resolution: Reorganization Plan No. II section4(f) transfers the Bureau of Biological Survey and its functions from Agriculture to Interior, and transfers the Secretary of Agriculture functions relating to wildlife, game and migratory birds to the Secretary of the Interior. Section401 transfers related departmental-head administration and section402 transfers records/property/personnel for administering those continuing functions. The June7,1939 joint resolution makes Plan II effective July1,1939, notwithstanding the general Reorganization Act timing; section2 does not extend preexisting durations. This is a legal administrative succession, not proof of physical delivery of records or property. It does not revoke the refuge, change its320-acre boundary, or terminate its wildlife/entry prohibition. Under the owner unnamed-instrument rule, this earlier instrument does not name EO8123 and is expressly disclosed and rejected as cessation. The continuing scopes remain subject to the later whole revocation on1958-08-05.

source.page_or_item: Reorganization Plan No. II, section4(f),4 FR2732, PDFpage6, left-column bottom continued at center-column top
source.quote:
(f) Bureau of Biological Survey.—The 
Bureau of Biological Survey in the De­
partment of Agriculture and its functions 
are hereby transferred to the Depart­
ment of the Interior and shall be ad­
ministered in that Department under the 
direction and supervision of the Secre­
tary of the Interior. The functions of 
the Secretary of Agriculture relating to 
the conservation of wild life, game, and 
migratory birds are hereby transferred 
to, and shall be exercised by, the Secre­
tary of the Interior. The provisions of 
the Act of May 18, 1934 (c. 299, 48 Stat. 
780), as amended by the Act of February 
8, 1936 (c. 40, 49 Stat. 1105), insofar as 
they relate to officers or employees of 
the Department of Agriculture desig­
nated by the Secretary of Agriculture to
enforce any act of Congress for the pro­
tection, preservation or restoration of 
game and other wild life and animals 
shall apply to officers and employees of 
the Department of the Interior desig­
nated by the Secretary of the Interior to 
exercise and discharge such duties.

sources.quote:
[Public Resolution No. 20—76th Congress] 
[S. J. Res. 138]
Joint Resolution Providing That Reorgan­
ization Plans Numbered I and II Shall 
Take Effect on July 1, 1939
Resolved by the Senate and House of 
Representatives of the United States of 
America in Congress assembled, That the 
provisions of reorganization plan numbered 
I, submitted to the Congress on April 25, 
1939, and the provisions of reorganization 
plan numbered n, submitted to the Con­
gress on May 9, 1939, shall take effect on July 
1, 1939, notwithstanding the provisions of 
the Reorganization Act of 1939.
Sec. 2. Nothing in such plans or this joint 
resolution shall be construed as having the 
effect of continuing any agency or function 
beyond the time when it would have ter­
minated without regard to such plans or 
this joint resolution or of continuing any 
function beyond the time when the agency 
in which it was vested would have terminated 
without regard to such plans or this joint 
resolution.
Wm. B. Bankhead
Speaker of the House of Representatives. 
Jno N Garner
Vice President of the United States and 
President of the Senate. 
Approved, June 7, 1939.
Franklin D Roosevelt

sources.page_or_item: Reorganization Plan No. II,sections401–402,4 FR2733,PDFpage7 left column
sources.quote:
Sec. 401. Transfer of Functions of 
Heads of Departments.—Except as other­
wise provided in this Plan, the functions 
of the head of any Department relating 
to the administration of any agency or 
function transferred from his Depart­
ment by this Plan, are hereby transferred 
to, and shall be exercised by, the head 
of the department or agency to which 
such transferred agency or function is 
transferred by this Plan.
Sec. 402; Transfer of Records, Prop­
erty, and Personnel.—All records and 
property (including office equipment) of 
the several agencies, and all records and 
property used primarily in the adminis­
tration of any functions, transferred by 
this Plan and, except as otherwise pro­
vided, all the personnel used in the ad­
ministration of such agencies and func­
tions (including officers whose chief 
duties relate to such administration) are 
hereby transferred to the respective de­
partments or agencies concerned, for use 
in the administration of the agencies and 
functions transferred by this Plan: Pro­
vided, That any personnel transferred to 
any department or agency by this sec­
tion found by the head of such depart­
ment or agency to be in excess of the 
personnel necessary for the administra­
tion of the functions transferred to his 
department or agency shall be retrans­
ferred under existing law to other posi­
tions in the Government service, or sepa­
rated from the service subject to the pro­
visions of section 10 (a) of the Reor­
ganization Act of 1939.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The original has no sunset, deadline, completed assignment or cessation condition. PR2416 changed only the refuge name on1940-07-25 and is recorded as amendment, not an ending. The1950 report documents damaged structures, water loss, virtual abandonment and removal of signs under verbal instructions; it does not cancel the refuge, terminate an easement, relinquish all federal control or supply an earlier legal ending. No earlier named cessation was located in bounded number/name searches. The complete original reserves320acres in N1/2section13,T143N,R78W,Fifth Principal Meridian. PLO1704 expressly revokes EO8123 and repeats the identical Lake Moraine tract. It has no partial limiter, deferred effective date or continuing provision. Its signature date is1958-08-05; NARA editorial1958-08-04 is contradicted by the actual center-column signature. FilingAug8/publicationAug9 are separate dates. The complete3paragraph inventory includes reservation, wildlife/entry prohibition with regulatory exception, and naming. Prohibition and regulation permission apply within this refuge; neither is an independent continuing command after whole revocation. PR2416 renaming does not create a new reservation or save EO8123 authority. No independent EO8123 command remains.

research_rationale: The complete official original and primary PLO1704 establish the reservation and all dependent protection/naming provisions ended by express whole revocation on1958-08-05. Primary pages correct both the contaminated frozen original inventory and the editorialAug4date. PR2416 supplies an earlier name amendment, not first cessation; the full1950 report supplies material operational abandonment evidence, not a legal termination. Original terms contain no lapse/completion mechanism and bounded later searches locate no revival or surviving EO-dependent norm. Reorganization Plan No. II section4(f) transfers the Bureau of Biological Survey and its functions from Agriculture to Interior, and transfers the Secretary of Agriculture functions relating to wildlife, game and migratory birds to the Secretary of the Interior. Section401 transfers related departmental-head administration and section402 transfers records/property/personnel for administering those continuing functions. The June7,1939 joint resolution makes Plan II effective July1,1939, notwithstanding the general Reorganization Act timing; section2 does not extend preexisting durations. This is a legal administrative succession, not proof of physical delivery of records or property. It does not revoke the refuge, change its320-acre boundary, or terminate its wildlife/entry prohibition. Under the owner unnamed-instrument rule, this earlier instrument does not name EO8123 and is expressly disclosed and rejected as cessation. The continuing scopes remain subject to the later whole revocation on1958-08-05.

savings_residuals.reason: Original subject-to-valid-rights language protects preexisting rights rather than granting surviving EO authority. PLO1704 contains no savings and states the lands are non-public lands, without a restoration/opening delay. Preexisting private rights, historical naming and independently authorized acts are not continuing EO effects under TC04/TC08. Bounded later checks found no revival or current EO-dependent residual.
